sections.html:
LaPorte County is in the northwest corner of Indiana, on the Lake Michigan shoreline. The city of La Porte is the county seat and Michigan City is the largest community. The 2020 census counted 112,417 people, and the 2025 estimate is 111,294, so the population has barely moved since 2010. About 71.4% of occupied homes are owner-occupied.

The county has 11 municipalities and 21 townships, the most of any Indiana county, so the township matters when you look up a parcel. Part of Indiana Dunes National Park lies inside the county, and lakes such as Clear Lake and Pine Lake in La Porte add recreation value. Michigan City draws visitors to its casino, outlet shopping and lakefront, while La Porte is built around county government and its school corporation.

Winters are long and snowy. La Porte averages about 65 inches of snow a year, mostly from December through February, and about 42.5 inches of precipitation. Average January lows are near 12 degrees.

Snow load, ice dams and frozen pipes are the practical worries for owners of older houses. Michigan City's summers are warm and humid, with frequent thunderstorms. If a roof or furnace is near the end of its life, a cash buyer takes that on as part of the purchase.

The county complex is at 809 State St., La Porte, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Most departments use the main number, 219-326-6808, with an extension.

The Treasurer also has an office at 555 Michigan Avenue, Suite 102 in La Porte. The county's tax page suggests starting an assessment question with the township assessor and reviewing the property record card first. The County Assessor oversees the township assessors, and Michigan Township has its own line at (219) 874-5611.

Watch the mailing date on your Form 11. Mailed before May 1, it sets a June 15 appeal deadline in that assessment year. Mailed later, or never sent, it moves the deadline to June 15 of the year the treasurer mails the bill.

Start with the township assessor. If you still disagree, the Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals owes you a hearing within 180 days of your petition, with at least 30 days of notice. Skipping a hearing without an approved continuance can cost $50.

For taxes payable in 2026 the standard homestead deduction is $48,000. After that it drops to $40,000, $30,000, $20,000 and $10,000 in the following years, and it ends with the 2030 assessment date. The supplemental deduction grows from 40% in 2026 to 62% in 2030 and 66.7% from 2031.

A homestead credit of the lesser of 10% of the bill or $300 started with 2026 taxes, and the over-65 credit is up to $150 for owners under the income limits. Applications for the over-65 credit are due by January 15 of the year the taxes are payable.

sections.h2: Township assessors and the property record card
sections.html:
With 21 townships, LaPorte County splits assessment work between the County Assessor and the township assessors. The County Assessor oversees the township assessors, and an assessment question usually starts at the township level. Before you call, pull your property record card. It lists what the county believes about your house, such as size, features and condition, and errors there carry straight into your value.

Compare the card with the house itself. If a garage, deck or finished basement is described wrongly, tell the assessor. Fixing the record before you list also means a buyer's lender or inspector sees consistent numbers.

sections.h2: What to bring and what to expect
sections.html:
Whichever office you visit, bring your tax bill or parcel number. Offices keep weekday hours, so plan around them: the county complex in La Porte runs 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

A typical sale with taxes owed runs in this order. You get a payoff figure, you sign a purchase agreement, the closing agent orders the title work, and at closing the tax and any fee are paid before you receive your proceeds. If the parcel has already been scheduled for the tax sale, the extra fee is part of that payoff, so ask for the number in writing.

If last year's spring installment is still unpaid, the parcel can be offered at the LaPorte County tax sale. October is the usual month. Notices start going out in late July, and the delinquent amount is typically due by mid-August.

  • Once a property is scheduled, a $220.00 administration fee is added.
  • Owner names and property details appear in the local newspaper and on the SRI Tax Sale Services website.
  • Bidders sign up with SRI ahead of the sale.
  • Redemption and procedure questions go to the Auditor at 219-326-6808 ext. 2004.
  • The Treasurer sends notice of surplus when a payment exceeds $5.00.

The county's real estate tax sale page has the current advertisement and parcel list.

You can pay at a Treasurer's office, at a local bank that accepts tax payments, or by mail with a federal postmark on or before the deadline. Some banks set earlier cutoffs. An owner who cannot pay in full can contact the Indiana Department of Revenue about a payment plan.

Taxes are due in two installments, in May and November. An owner who sells with a balance outstanding usually has the closing agent pay it from the proceeds. Anyone with an unpaid spring installment should look at the tax sale timeline above, because a parcel can become eligible after the prior spring installment goes unpaid.

sections.h2: Steps for a seller with unpaid tax
sections.html:
Taxes owed do not block a sale, but timing matters because of the October sale window. This order of steps keeps things moving.

  1. Call the Treasurer in Michigan City at 219-874-5611 ext. 2062, or the La Porte office, and ask for the amount owed.
  2. Ask the Auditor at 219-326-6808 ext. 2004 whether the parcel is on the sale list and whether the $220.00 fee has been added.
  3. Look at the property record card and, if the value looks wrong, call the township assessor before the June 15 window closes.
  4. Give the closing agent the figures so the payoff comes out of your proceeds.
  5. If you cannot pay and still want to keep the house, ask the Department of Revenue about a payment plan.

A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands can often close before the sale date. The balance, the fee and any penalties are still paid from the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: When is the LaPorte County property tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: June 15. If the Form 11 notice was mailed before May 1, it is June 15 of that assessment year. Later notices move the deadline to June 15 of the year the bill is mailed.

faqs.q: Where is the LaPorte County Treasurer?
faqs.a: The Treasurer has an office at 555 Michigan Avenue, Suite 102 in La Porte, plus one at 300 Washington Street, #361 in Michigan City. The county line is 219-326-6808.

faqs.q: When is the LaPorte County tax sale?
faqs.a: The county typically holds the sale in October. Notices go out beginning in late July.

faqs.q: How much is the LaPorte County tax sale fee?
faqs.a: A $220.00 tax sale administration fee is added once a property is scheduled for sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell a LaPorte County house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax balance can usually be paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
